newsitem.title: USA: Countrywide Credit Sept loans decline.
newsitem.headline: Countrywide Credit Sept loans decline.

text.p: Countrywide Credit Industries Inc said Thursday that the company funded $2.7 billion of mortgage loans in September 1996, 11 percent lower than the $3.0 billion funded in September 1995.
The company's pipeline of loans in process totaled $4.2 billion at September 30, 1996, compared to $5.3 billion at September 30, 1995.
In the loan production sector, both sub-prime loan production of $77 million and home equity loan fundings of $53 million established new company records, the company said.

It added that there were two fewer business days in September than in August. Average daily applications increased modestly month to month and total monthly production declined 12 percent, partially reflecting the shorter month."

The company's servicing portfolio increased to $150 billion at September 30, 1996, 16 percent higher than the $130 billion portfolio at September 30, 1995. The portfolio had a weighted average coupon of 7.8 percent at the end of both September 1996 and September 1995.

Countrywide's fixed-rate loan production amounted to $1.9 billion in September 1996, or 71 percent of total production, and $2.4 billion, or 78 percent of total production, in September 1995. Purchase mortgage activity was $2.1 billion in September 1996 and $2.0 billion in September 1995. Refinances represented 23 percent of total fundings in September 1996 compared to 35 percent in September 1995.

The company funded $53 million of home equity loans in September 1996 and $19 million in September 1995. Sub-prime loan funding activity was $77 million in September 1996 and $2 million in September 1995.
